title: CAS to TAS and density altitude above the tropopause, ISA+10
who: Pilots, dispatchers, flight-test and performance engineers
why_hard: Three things must all be right: the isothermal (stratosphere) pressure law above 36,089 ft, the compressible CAS-to-Mach relation (not CAS/sqrt(sigma)), and the actual ISA+10 temperature for the speed of sound. Density altitude above the tropopause needs the isothermal density law; the 120 ft per deg C rule of thumb does not hold there.
failure_cost: Wrong TAS feeds fuel planning and navigation; wrong density altitude feeds engine and buffet margins.
sources: ICAO Doc 7488/3, Manual of the ICAO Standard Atmosphere
Subsonic compressible pitot-static relations (e.g. Gracey, NASA RP-1046, Measurement of Aircraft Speed and Altitude, 1980)
